Replace the data in a toolkit lab

Source: R/toolkit-lab.R
swap_lab_data.Rd

Swaps the responses behind a lab made with new_lab() for another dataset, for example next year's class or your own test. The lab's text, answer checks and questions are computed from the data, so nothing else needs to change. Settings you leave out (group, data_title, story) are kept from the current data, except that items and key are always worked out again. The item_info and scores of the AI sections are kept unless you give new ones. Run check_material() afterwards.

Usage

swap_lab_data(
  lab,
  data,
  items = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  key = NULL,
  item_info = NULL,
  scores = NULL,
  data_title = NULL,
  story = NULL
)

Arguments

lab

the lab folder.

data

the responses: A data frame or matrix, or the path of a file (.csv, .tsv, .txt, .xlsx, .xls, .sav, .dta, .sas7bdat or .rds). Items must be scored 0/1 or in ordered integer categories, unless you give a key. A frequency table (one row per response pattern with a freq or count column, such as mirt::LSAT7) is expanded to one row per person.

items

the item columns, by name or position. By default, every column whose values are whole numbers from 0 to 9 (other than group and ID-like columns), or the names of a named key.

group

optional grouping variable with two values, for the DIF section: A column name of data, or a vector with one value per row.

key

optional answer key for unscored multiple-choice responses, one value per item; the items are scored with mirt::key2binary().

item_info

optional data frame (or the path of a data file) with one row per item, for the AI sections. It needs a column item (or id) with the item names used in data. A stem column (and, for multiple-choice items, option columns A to E and a key column with the letter of the keyed option) enables the "item-features" section; a family column naming each item's item model or family enables the "aig" section.

scores

optional data frame (or the path of a data file) of machine scores of constructed responses, for the "ai-scoring" section: One row per scored response, with columns machine and human1 (the human score, NA where no person read the response) and, optionally, human2 (a second reading), group (for fairness checks), item and period (an administration or engine version, for drift checks). Rename your columns to these names first.

data_title

a short name for the data used in the lab's text, for example "the Grade 8 science test".

story

a paragraph that sets the scene, shown at the start of the lab.

Value

The lab folder, invisibly.

Details

If the lab has a DIF section and the new data have no group, the DIF section will fail; remove it with remove_lab_section().

See also

new_lab(), lab_data()

Examples

course <- file.path(tempdir(), "swap-demo")
lab <- new_lab("demo", data = expand.table(LSAT7), course = course,
               sections = c("intro", "classical"))
swap_lab_data(lab, data = expand.table(LSAT6), data_title = "the LSAT section 6 items")
lab_data(file.path(lab, "data"))$info$data_title
#> [1] "the LSAT section 6 items"
